cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I said the evening would flow, I was plainly describing this kitchen flood. You may stop looking surprised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant the conversation would flow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And what are we talking about? Water. Put that beside my original words before you dispute the forecast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't predict a burst pipe. Help me turn the water off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You take the valve; I'll clear the doorway. Once it stops flowing, you can tell me which part of my description was inaccurate.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares flow predicted flood and controls B reaction; A3 commands comparison with original words; A5 assigns repair roles while inviting only a challenge A frames as impossible.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 conversation correction to make water its subject; A5 uses B4 water-off request to direct repair and renew the same flow prediction.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects original meaning and B4 asks urgent help, giving B an actual task beyond rebuttal.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 repair request to preserve authority even while helping, returning to flow after the valve is shut rather than new earlier words.

specificity.evidence: A1 kitchen flood and B4 burst pipe make valve/doorway actions ordinary emergency responses; no sentient plumbing premise needed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 practical role division keeps the retrospective certainty in the same interaction rather than a detached pun.
